title: Reproducibility package for 'Two-year agreement of a low handgrip strength classification in 9116 Chinese adults: a single reading should not be reported as a persistent state'
description:
Changes in this version (1.0.13)

  • Archival metadata aligned with the final submitted manuscript title: Two-year agreement of a low handgrip strength classification in 9116 Chinese adults: a single reading should not be reported as a persistent state. The previous record used a thousands separator and described a single reading as a provisional label; the manuscript now states that a single reading should not be reported as a persistent state.
  • .zenodo.json, CITATION.cff and README.md carry the same title; the version field is 1.0.13. The concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23677282 is unchanged and resolves to this version.
  • No script, estimate, exhibit or pipeline step changed. No CHARLS microdata are included.

Changes in this version (1.0.12)

  • code/jfa_20_cutoff_table.R added: the generator of Supplementary Table S41, two-year reproduction under the AWGS 2019, EWGSOP2 and FNIH cut-offs in the 6,052-person landmark sample. It reads out/jamda_full.rds (built by 01_build.R) and writes out/S41_three_cutoffs.csv. Its gate checks the published AWGS row (647 low in 2011; 40.5%, 35.6-45.6; kappa 0.30), so it is deliberately not a step of run_all.sh: on the synthetic cohort those published values are a structural smoke test, not a reproduction.
  • The archived title now matches the current manuscript title (Two-year agreement of a low handgrip strength classification in 9,116 Chinese adults: a single reading is a provisional label); CITATION.cff was corrected in the same way.
  • No estimate reported in the manuscript or supplementary tables changed. No figure or submission document was added: this package ships the code and aggregate inputs that regenerate the exhibits, and its .gitignore excludes manuscripts and reviewer correspondence.

Changes in this version (1.0.11)

  • code/99_stratum_bench_2025.R moved out of code/charls_only/ and added to run_all.sh as the step after 96_stratum_bench.R. It reads only out/jamda_full.rds, so it never needed the CHARLS release; the pipeline now exercises it on the synthetic cohort (57 steps).
  • On the synthetic cohort the step reports that its rows are a structural smoke test, and checks the published values (59.5 / 67.8 / 52.1 / 57.3) only when the cohort is the CHARLS one (n = 6,052).
  • No estimate reported in the manuscript changed.

Changes in this version (1.0.10)

  • code/charls_only/99_stratum_bench_2025.R added: the no-change benchmark under the 2025 age-specific cut-offs. In the 50-64 band it expects 57.3% (95% simulation interval 42.9-71.8) against 63.7% observed, which is the comparison reported in the Results. 96_stratum_bench.R runs the same model at the AWGS 2019 cut-offs only, so this figure had no archived generator.
  • manifest/s27/JFA_stratum_bench_2025.csv holds the seven rows of that run; the script reproduces the file byte for byte.
  • manifest/outputs.csv maps Table S27 to both benchmark scripts and to this output.
  • No estimate reported in the manuscript changed.

Changes in this version (1.0.9)

  • code/73_rev16_calib.R added as the generator of Supplementary Table S14: C1 55.6% (95% simulation interval 52.5-58.9), C2 59.5% (56.2-62.9), C3 58.6% (55.2-61.8). The manifest had attributed S14 to 22_null_sim.R, which implements only the C1 specification.
  • code/85_figure2_bars.py and code/86_figure3_distance.py redraw the two submitted figures from the aggregate inputs in manifest/fig_inputs/; both reproduce the submitted files pixel for pixel.
  • manifest/outputs.csv now maps Figure 2 to its current generator, adds Figure 3 and adds Table S28. Tables S29-S31 and S33-S36 still have no row: their generators exist but none names the table, and a guessed mapping would repeat the S14 error.
  • No estimate reported in the manuscript changed.

Changes in this version (1.0.8)

  • Two scripts added under code/charls_only/: 98_full_awgs_icc.R regenerates Supplementary Tables S37 and S38 (the complete AWGS 2019 possible-sarcopenia definition in the full 6,052-person analytic sample, and the short-interval ICC 0.80-0.99 sensitivity), and 99_full_awgs_cc.R runs the chair-stand complete-case check. Four summary CSVs are archived under manifest/s37_s38/.
  • The archived title now matches the current manuscript title (Two-year agreement of a low handgrip reading in 6,052 Chinese adults); the previous record still carried the pre-revision title.
  • No estimate reported in the manuscript changed. No CHARLS microdata are included: the shipped CSVs are aggregate tables of 3-17 rows.

Changes in this version (1.0.7)

  • CITATION.cff still carried the pre-revision title and version: 1.0.5. Corrected, so the citation that GitHub and Zenodo surface matches the archived version.
  • DATA_AVAILABILITY.md quoted a passage naming version 1.0.5 and the DOI of that version. The quoted statement now uses the concept DOI and names the version described, so it cannot go stale when a new version is archived.
  • The descriptive sentence in this metadata still described the pre-revision study. Rewritten.
  • No script, estimate or exhibit changed. Version 1.0.6 introduced code/charls_only/97_s28_dominant_2025.R and is archived as 10.5281/zenodo.23917161.

Changes in this version (1.0.6)

  • New script code/charls_only/97_s28_dominant_2025.R generates Supplementary Table S28: the 2025 age-specific thresholds applied to the AWGS dominant-hand reading rather than to the maximum of four trials. It rebuilds the dominant-hand value from the trial-level fields qc002-qc006 and returns prevalence, two-year reversion, paired differences with community-cluster bootstrap intervals, and reclassification counts, by age stratum and for the 2019 and 2025 cut-offs.
  • Result reported in Section 4.5: at ages 50-64 the dominant-hand rule classifies 2.5 percentage points more participants as low (ratio 1.19, 95% CI 1.9-3.1) and two-year reversion is 2.3 points lower (ratio 0.96, 95% CI -4.8 to 0.3). The direction of the paper's conclusion is unchanged.
  • Title updated to the title of the revised manuscript.
  • No estimate reported elsewhere in the manuscript changed.

Code, specification and simulated data for a cohort study of how often a low grip reading is reproduced two years later, and of whether the earlier reading adds prognostic value beyond the current one.

Contents

  • 57 R scripts and five Python utilities, plus a shared R helper library (code/lib.R), five further R scripts that need the CHARLS release (code/charls_only/) (code/): cohort construction, agreement and measurement-error analyses, the weighted multiple-imputation models, the incremental-value models, the bounding analysis, the frailty index, calibration, the figure and table builders
  • Analysis specification (_supp.md), written after the primary analysis was run and archived with it
  • A deterministic synthetic-data generator. The simulated cohort itself is not distributed: a one-row-per-person file is structurally indistinguishable from the micro data the CHARLS terms prohibit redistributing, so the package ships the generator and the guard that enforces this
  • Fitted model objects (model/fit_store.rds), so the standardised five-year risks in Supplementary Table S6 can be recomputed without respondent data
  • SHA-256 checksums of the CHARLS inputs used (manifest/)

No CHARLS data are included or redistributed. The CHARLS terms of agreement prohibit publishing original micro data in any form; registered users can obtain the release identified in manifest/inputs.sha256 from the CHARLS website. The synthetic cohort has the same structure, variable names and missingness but is simulated: it does not reproduce the published estimates, and exists to show that the code runs.

Changes in this version (1.0.5)

  • Five scripts added so that every supplementary table has a generator: 91b_hetero_stratified.R (Table S25, the no-change benchmark with the error estimated by distance to the cut-off), 93_rev29_boot.R (design effect of resampling communities rather than individuals), 94_rev29_hmm2.R (Table S26, the two-state latent Markov model), 95_rev31_age.R (Table S27) and 96_stratum_bench.R (the stratum-specific benchmark quoted in Section 3.2). Tables S24-S27 had no script in 1.0.4: the manuscript cited them while the package that the Data Availability statement points to could not regenerate them.
  • New exhibit: Table S27, agreement and two-year reversion by age stratum, with the AWGS 2025 age-specific thresholds applied to the 50-64 stratum.
  • run_all.sh runs 56 steps: 54 R scripts and two Python utilities.
  • No estimate reported in the manuscript changed.

Changes in this version (1.0.4)

  • share_align.py read out/jamda_full.csv through an absolute path left over from the analysis directory (E://workbuddy//...//analysis//out//jamda_full.csv). Every other script in the package addresses its inputs relatively, and this one did not, so the step failed on any machine but the author's: the pipeline ended 50 of 51 on CI, the one failure being this script, three steps after 01_build.R writes the file it wanted. The path is now out/jamda_full.csv and the full pipeline passes 51 of 51 on the synthetic cohort.
  • No analysis, number or exhibit changed. Version 1.0.3 is archived as 10.5281/zenodo.23730913 and keeps the absolute path; this release exists only to make the cited version runnable off the machine it was written on.

Changes in this version (1.0.3)

  • Ten scripts added so that every exhibit in Tables S1-S23 has a script: 31_rev9_errorsim.R, 51_rev11_extra.R, 60_s21_landmark.R, 61_s21_boot.R, 62_s21_adjust.R, 63_s21_panelC.R, 80b_m3_adl_missing.R, 80c_m3_desc.R, 81_figure2_rev23.R and 82_rev23_jiang_reconcile.R, plus share_align.py
  • Two scripts that read the CHARLS release rather than the synthetic cohort (80_rev23_review.R, _probe_recon.R) are now included in code/charls_only/, with a note on how to run them
  • New exhibit: Table S23, the participants whose 2013 ADL block was entirely missing
  • The description of model/fit_store.rds now names Supplementary Table S6, which is what it reproduces
  • Two scripts added that regenerate the two submitted figures exactly: 83_figure1_rev28.py (Figure 1, the cohort flow, which had no generator in 1.0.2) and 84_figure2_rev28.R (Figure 2 in its submitted layout; the values are those of 07b_figure2.R). Neither is a step in run_all.sh: they need matplotlib and R cairo, and they overwrite the pipeline's figure output with the submitted layout. Figure 1 and Figure 2 in manifest/outputs.csv now point at them.

Changes in version 1.0.2

  • Eight scripts added so that every exhibit in the manuscript and the supplementary tables can be regenerated from this package: 30_rev9_incremental.R, 32_rev9_boot.R, 40_share_vs_charls.R, 44_extra.R, 48_lca.R, 50_rev11_review.R, 60_rev14_spline.R and 70_rev15_decomp.R. Version 1.0.1 disclosed six exhibits (S9-S13, S15) as not reproducible from the archive; they now run in the pipeline.
  • run_all.sh runs 40 steps: 39 R scripts and the table builder.

Changes in this version (1.0.1)

  • Title updated to the title of the revised manuscript.
  • Four scripts added for the analyses introduced in revision: 73_bounding_mi.R (bounding of the loss to follow-up), 74_frailty_mi.R (frailty index excluding grip), 72_calibration.R (cross-validated calibration) and 75_kappa_cluster.R (kappa interval by community bootstrap).
  • Version 1.0.0 advertised a synthetic CSV that it did not include. The claim has been corrected rather than the file added: the repository guard rejects row-level files, synthetic or not.
  • The synthetic generator now emits da002, which the frailty index counts.
  • Kappa intervals in Table 1 resample communities rather than individuals; the design effect of that change is 1.40.
